average-precision.inputs_code:
n = 2000
labels = (rng.random(n) < 0.03).astype(float)
labels[:3] = 1.0
# Two-decimal scores: blocks of tied rows, so the tie rule is tested.
scores = np.round(rng.beta(2, 5, n) + 0.3 * labels * rng.random(n), 2)
inputs = (labels, scores)

bmr-threshold.inputs_code:
n = 400
amounts = np.round(rng.lognormal(3.5, 1.3, n), 2)
# Scores of a model that kept 3,000 of 59,700 genuine rows (beta ~ 5%).
p_s = rng.beta(0.6, 3, n)
beta = 3_000 / 59_700
labels = (rng.random(n) < beta * p_s / (beta * p_s - p_s + 1)).astype(np.int64)
labels[:3] = 1
inputs = (amounts, labels, p_s, 300, 59_700, 3_000, np.array([1.0, 5.0, 20.0]))

card-precision-top-k.inputs_code:
counts = rng.poisson(1.5, (7, 60)).ravel()
days = np.repeat(np.repeat(np.arange(7), 60), counts)
cards = np.repeat(np.tile(np.arange(60), 7), counts)
compromised = np.isin(cards, rng.choice(60, 14, replace=False))
labels = (compromised & (rng.random(len(days)) < 0.5)).astype(np.int64)
scores = rng.random(len(days)) + 0.6 * labels * rng.random(len(days))
perm = rng.permutation(len(days))
inputs = (days[perm], cards[perm], scores[perm], labels[perm], 4)

prequential-selection.inputs_code:
counts = rng.poisson(0.6, (41, 150)).ravel()
days = np.repeat(np.repeat(np.arange(41), 150), counts)
cards = np.repeat(np.tile(np.arange(150), 41), counts)
labels = np.zeros(len(days), dtype=np.int64)
for d0 in range(41):
    for card in rng.choice(150, 2, replace=False):
        window = (cards == card) & (days >= d0) & (days < d0 + 6)
        labels[window & (rng.random(len(days)) < 0.5)] = 1
# One feature, informative through its magnitude: frauds sit in both
# tails. A candidate is a number of quantile bins of a histogram model.
x = rng.normal(0, 1, len(days)) + labels * rng.choice([-2.5, 2.5], len(days))

def fit_and_score(train_idx, n_bins):
    edges = np.quantile(x[train_idx], np.linspace(0, 1, n_bins + 1)[1:-1])
    b = np.searchsorted(edges, x[train_idx])
    rate = ((np.bincount(b, weights=labels[train_idx], minlength=n_bins) + 0.5)
            / (np.bincount(b, minlength=n_bins) + 1.0))
    return rate[np.searchsorted(edges, x)] + 1e-6 * x

inputs = (days, cards, labels, [1, 2, 4, 8, 32], fit_and_score, 30, 3, 5, 3, 4, 3)

prequential-split.inputs_code:
n = 600
days = np.sort(rng.integers(0, 30, n))
cards = rng.integers(0, 25, n)
labels = np.zeros(n, dtype=np.int64)
for card, first in zip(rng.choice(25, 14, replace=False), rng.integers(0, 26, 14)):
    window = (cards == card) & (days >= first) & (days < first + 8)
    labels[window & (rng.random(n) < 0.6)] = 1
inputs = (days, cards, labels, 14, 3, 5, 3, 4)

savings-metric.inputs_code:
n = 200
amounts = np.round(rng.lognormal(3.5, 1.0, n), 2)
labels = np.zeros(n, dtype=np.int64)
frauds = rng.choice(n, 6, replace=False)
labels[frauds] = 1
decisions = (rng.random(n) < 0.08).astype(np.int64)
decisions[frauds[:2]] = 1
# €0.25 makes flagging everything the cheaper trivial policy; €5 and
# €40 make it flagging nothing.
c_a = np.array([0.25, 5.0, 40.0])
inputs = (amounts, labels, decisions, c_a)
